results.description: Chat is the first primary navigation entry above Agents
Clicking Chat opens the New chat composer
New chat defaults: built-in assistant (no agent picker), remembered model, temp workspace
Model menu: search, Recent pairs, runtime rows; runtime opens its models to the side
A not-yet-loaded runtime shows loading, then its models
Grok Build is an available runtime with its own models by default
Search is cross-runtime and labels each result with its runtime
Choosing a result updates the button and closes the menu
Reasoning effort is a separate control
Skills: "/" opens a ranked skill menu (bare "/" lists all), Enter or click tags it; chips removable
Workspace picker: temp default, existing folders, open another folder
Quick pick restores a recent runtime+model in one click
Sending the first message starts a chat run and opens it
Mid-chat picker keeps the runtime and switches the model
The product right panel (all workspace tool tabs) is hidden by default and opens on demand
No chat ⋯ menu; archive/delete stay on the tree row (with confirmation)
Clicking a single-agent run in the tree opens it in the chat view (Option B)
+ on an agent in the tree starts a new chat: assistant by default, or that agent shown as a removable chip
A skill tag alone can be sent; it is sent as the instruction only
"@" addresses an agent or team; a team chat uses one shared model/workspace and opens in the real Team view
Chats follow the normal Workspaces tree rules: workspaces by name, collapsed unless holding the open chat, agents under each workspace
Auto-approve is on by default in every workspace, can be turned off, and the chat header shows the mode
The pencil on the Chat menu item opens a fresh New chat; no separate New chat row
Agents catalog is unchanged and still reachable
Catalog error shows retry and recovers
Scenario: a runtime missing on this machine reads Not installed with its reason and cannot open
First run: no chats, no quick picks, AutoByteus default model
Narrow: composer controls wrap without overflow; picker fits the viewport
